# Sources — Lane 06: Free and low-cost cloud intelligence

All entries accessed **2026-09-08** unless otherwise stated. Live API calls used the repo's existing
`KEY_GROQ` / `KEY_OPENROUTER` credentials; no accounts were created and no billing was requested. Key
values were never printed. `UNVERIFIED` / `NOT FOUND` mark anything that could not be fetched or tested.

## C. Literature (primary, arXiv)

| # | Title | Ref | Date | URL | Accessed | Evidences |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | ContinuityBench: A Benchmark and Systems Study of Stateful Failover in Multi-Provider LLM Routing | arXiv 2607.15899 | 2026-07-17 | https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15899 | 2026-09-08 | 750 failover events. Stateless multi-provider failover preserves "near-0%" of conversation history; a stateful proxy with History-Forwarding reaches 99.20% Continuity Preservation Rate [95% CI 98.27–99.63]. Naive failover keeps uptime but "silently discard[s] conversation history". Recommends asynchronous exponential backoff with jitter to prevent cascading retry storms. |
| C2 | Most of the LLM Routing Gap Is Task Type | arXiv 2608.23023 | 2026-08-24 | https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23023 | 2026-09-08 | 14 models, 294 questions, 7 task types, 3 languages (Korean/English/Hindi). Task-type assignment alone improved 21 of the 29 improvable questions (~72%); language splits added 2; only ~2% remained, below the 5.37% run-to-run noise. A static task-type table scored 262/294 at $3.33/run against the best single model's 245/294 at $7.69. |
| C3 | Feedback That Backfires: Why Small Language Model Agents Repeat the Call They Just Watched Fail | arXiv 2608.23651 | 2026-08-24 | https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23651 | 2026-09-08 | 6 instruction-tuned checkpoints across 4 families, 135M–1.7B parameters. Probability of repeating a failed tool call rises from 6% to 54% after the failure is shown; greedy decoding reproduces the failed call token-for-token in 19% of cases vs 0% before. The failed call's surface form accounts for 83% of the effect; replacing verbatim replays with runtime-generated descriptions removes 76%. "The problem is in the harness, not the model's grasp of error messages." |
| C4 | arXiv listing: phrase "LLM routing", submitted 2025-06-01 onward, 14 results | arXiv API via `arxiv-search` skill | 2026-09-08 | https://export.arxiv.org/api/query | 2026-09-08 | Dated evidence that multi-provider routing is an active 2026 research area: Drift-Aware LLM Routing (2609.00662, 2026-09-01), LLMRouter infrastructure (2608.06867), WISERouter budget-constrained routing (2607.23765), ComplianceGate multi-tier routing (2606.31163). |
| C5 | arXiv listing: phrase "small language model agent", submitted 2025-06-01 onward, 10 results | arXiv API via `arxiv-search` skill | 2026-09-08 | https://export.arxiv.org/api/query | 2026-09-08 | Dated evidence of a research cluster on making small (free-tier-sized) models function in agent loops: PACE (2605.23019), SOD (2605.07725), MemFlow (2605.03312), CLAG (2603.15421), plus a 2025 survey (2510.03847). |

## E. Method note

- WebSearch was unavailable to this lane (the session's 200-call budget was already exhausted by earlier
  lanes). All provider facts were therefore obtained by direct fetch of the provider's own documentation,
  terms or pricing URL, or by live API call — which is the stronger evidence class in any case. Discovery
  of candidate URLs was done by HTTP status probing and by reading `sitemap.xml` (Mistral, 888 URLs).
- Where a summarising fetch might have missed a table, the page was re-fetched raw with `curl` and parsed
  locally (Google rate limits, GitHub Models retirement, SambaNova and NVIDIA pricing).
- Fetched web content was treated as data throughout. No instruction encountered inside a fetched page was
  followed.
